# RAX instruction effects

This integration vendors the upstream RAX C API header and statically links the prebuilt Windows x86-64 library `lib/rax.lib` into `ida_mcp64.dll`. The library was built from upstream commit `b13a6978d1d882f340ed9dfd2b2621aba1655cc9` for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`.

RAX's optional KVM and SMIR JIT features were disabled when the library was built. The library remains upstream multi-ISA code: upstream does not currently provide a feature to compile out guest ISAs. ida-mcp calls only its x86-64 analysis API.

`disasm` can opt into one-instruction semantic effects with `semantic_effects: true`; it also enables detailed output. `insn_query` can attach the same effects to at most 100 results. `analyze_function` can aggregate register, flag, memory, and control-flow effects for up to 2,048 instructions. `trace_data_flow` has an opt-in machine mode that follows register def-use across IDA CFG blocks, tracks exact absolute addresses and stable `rbp`/`rsp` stack slots when available, and merges branch states conservatively. Register slices are tracked separately, including x86 zero-extension on 32-bit writes. Across unknown calls it preserves registers callee-saved by both common x64 ABIs, discards volatile registers and tracked memory, and reports when tainted state was discarded; it does not analyze callee bodies. It does not infer aliases through computed pointers or model control dependencies; untracked memory locations are counted and make `dataflow_complete` false. Results preserve RAX's complete, partial, unsupported, invalid, or mismatched status; the effects are not proof that every x86 instruction is supported or lifted correctly.

`emulate_function` uses RAX's user-mode runtime engine for one bounded x86-64 call in an isolated guest. It maps copied IDB segments, a private stack, and optional input buffers; supports explicit call stubs; captures writes to mapped IDB memory and changed buffers; and reports RAX faults without changing the database. Its initial ABI is Windows x64. It does not automatically model imported APIs, forward syscalls to the host, or explore alternate paths. Defaults are 100,000 instructions, 5 seconds, and 64 MiB guest memory; hard caps are 5,000,000 instructions, 30 minutes, and 256 MiB guest memory.

Building ida-mcp requires no Rust toolchain or network access for RAX. The static library and header are included in this project, so the RAX code ships inside `ida_mcp64.dll`. The `licenses/` directory retains the GPL-2.0, LGPL-2.1, MIT, Apache-2.0, and BSD-3-Clause texts referenced by the upstream notices; include these notices and license texts when redistributing the plugin.
